Teamtailor pricing is quote-only in 2026, with nothing listed on the website. Vendr's February 2026 buyer guide estimates list prices from $300-$400 per month on Starter up to $1,500+ per month on Enterprise. Negotiated deals land lower, at roughly $250-$400/mo for small teams and $1,200-$2,000+/mo for large ones. That works out to about $3,000 to $24,000+ per year, with most mid-market contracts in the $6,000-$12,000 range.

What's the catch? Despite promising unlimited users and unlimited job postings, Teamtailor still sends every buyer into a sales conversation without a number. Vendr's estimates tier plans by active job openings ("job slots"), and most agreements carry 3-8% annual renewal escalators that compound over a multi-year term.

This guide breaks down Teamtailor pricing 2026 by team size, maps the hidden costs buyers see only at negotiation, explains when teams decide to move off Teamtailor, and compares it to five alternatives. If you're also evaluating other platforms, our [Ashby pricing breakdown](https://www.pin.com/blog/ashby-pricing/) and [Workable pricing breakdown](https://www.pin.com/blog/workable-pricing/) cover those in the same detail.

> **TL;DR:**
>
> - **Quote-only pricing, roughly $300-$1,500+/mo at list.** [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/teamtailor) (2026) estimates Starter at $300-$400/mo, Growth at $600-$1,200/mo, and Enterprise at $1,500+/mo. Teamtailor's own pricing page shows no numbers.
> - **Unlimited users and jobs, but tiers track hiring volume.** Teamtailor quotes by company size, while Vendr's buyer data maps tiers to concurrent open roles (5-10, 10-30, 30+). Fast-scaling teams can outgrow a tier between renewals.
> - **No free plan, annual terms, 3-8% escalators.** A $12,000 contract at a 5% escalator becomes $13,230 by year three. Negotiate a cap or flat renewal rate at signing.
> - **Key features sit above Starter.** Buyer reports place AI Co-pilot, nurture campaigns, and SSO on higher tiers, so most mid-market teams land in the $600-$1,200/mo Growth range.
> - **No built-in candidate sourcing.** Teamtailor tracks applicants but won't find passive talent. For sourcing-focused teams, [Pin](https://www.pin.com/) has a free plan, paid plans from $99/mo, and 850M+ profiles, with no limit on active positions.

## What Does Teamtailor Actually Cost in 2026?

Without a public price list, all Teamtailor cost data comes from its sales team or third-party buyer databases. According to [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/teamtailor) (2026), negotiated prices run from about $250/month for small teams to $2,000+/month for large deployments, and mid-market buyers typically spend $6,000-$12,000 per year in total. Only one public price point exists: a [UK government G-Cloud listing](https://www.applytosupply.digitalmarketplace.service.gov.uk/g-cloud/services/930243870190479) at £1,250 per unit per year, and that listing doesn't define the unit.

Here's what companies are actually paying, based on Vendr's negotiated-price data (Teamtailor ATS pricing by team size):

<figure style="margin:2rem 0;padding:0;line-height:0"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Range bar chart of Teamtailor negotiated annual cost by team size" style="width:100%;height:auto;display:block;border-radius:12px"></figure>

A few things to know about how Teamtailor charges:

-   **Quote-based, scaled to company size.** Teamtailor's pricing page splits its offer between small and midsize companies (up to 1,000 employees) and enterprises (1,000+). Every plan includes unlimited users and unlimited job postings.
-   **Job slots drive the buyer-reported tiers.** Vendr's estimates map Starter to 5-10 active openings, Growth to 10-30, and Enterprise to 30+. Expect your quote to reflect how many roles you hire for at once.
-   **Annual escalators.** Most contracts include a 3-8% automatic price increase at renewal, per Vendr. This is negotiable at signing - push for a cap or flat renewal rate.
-   **No free plan.** The trial typically runs 14 days and can be extended on request, but a sales rep sets it up rather than a self-serve sign-up.

**We've noticed** a consistent pattern among recruiting teams that evaluate Teamtailor: tiered pricing looks affordable until you're mid-hiring-surge. Teams that model their contract around 10 concurrent roles often get a shock when hiring accelerates. Push past the top of your tier and the next renewal quote is priced for the bigger one.

Recruiting teams most surprised by Teamtailor's total costs tend to have unpredictable or seasonal hiring cycles. Steady-state hiring at 5-10 roles fits comfortably in the Starter or low Growth budget. Fast-growing companies running multi-department searches often find costs drifting toward Enterprise's $1,500+/mo ($18,000+/yr) before they realize it. That's the inflection point where teams start evaluating alternatives. Platforms that don't charge more when hiring picks up - or that include sourcing in the base cost - become appealing.

Tiering by open roles creates a pricing quirk worth understanding. A 200-person company that only hires for 5 roles at a time could land in a lower tier than a 30-person startup with 15 open positions. That makes Teamtailor unusually affordable for large companies with steady, low-volume hiring - but expensive for fast-growing startups running multiple searches. Model your typical concurrent openings before requesting a quote, not just your headcount.

AI Co-pilot and nurture campaigns are both locked out of Starter, and Teamtailor has spent 2026 adding Co-pilot features such as job-ad editing and analytics reports, according to its product news page. If you're hiring regularly, those capabilities matter, which makes $600-$1,200/mo a more realistic starting point than the $300-$400/mo Starter estimate.

## What Are the Hidden Costs?

Buyer-reported data from [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/teamtailor) (2026) shows Teamtailor's headline quote rarely reflects the total cost of ownership. Several costs only surface during negotiation or after signing.

Here are the costs buyers report being surprised by:

-   **Onboarding fees: $1,000-$5,000.** Vendr lists onboarding in this range for managed setup (data import, career site build, integration configuration). Ask for the cost breakdown before signing.
-   **Tier jumps when hiring spikes.** Because buyer-reported tiers track concurrent openings, a seasonal spike from 10 to 30 roles can move you from Growth pricing toward Enterprise. This catches seasonal employers off guard.
-   **Integration gaps.** Reviewers on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/144801/Teamtailor/reviews/) flag missing native connections, such as Google Meet for video interviews, which can mean paying for a separate tool.
-   **Annual renewal escalators.** Most contracts include 3-8% automatic price increases at renewal. On a $12,000/yr contract, that's $360-$960 more each year without adding any features.

Here's why the escalator clause matters so much. A $12,000/yr contract with a 5% annual escalator reaches $13,230 in year three and $14,586 in year five. Over the first three years, that's about $1,830 more than three flat years would cost. At 8%, the same contract passes $16,300 by year five. To avoid this, negotiate a flat renewal rate or a 3% cap during initial contract discussions.

## What Are Teamtailor's Biggest Limitations?

Teamtailor holds a 4.6/5 rating across 113 reviews on [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/144801/Teamtailor/reviews/) (2026), and most feedback is positive. The complaints that do recur point to specific gaps that matter more for some buyers than others.

Here are the most common limitations reported by users:

-   **No published pricing.** Every buyer starts from zero in the sales conversation. You can't compare Teamtailor to alternatives without first giving the sales team your contact info and sitting through a demo. That's friction most mid-market buyers don't want.
-   **Reporting and analytics gaps.** Reviewers call analytics a weak spot and say data export is harder than it should be. Teamtailor added Co-pilot-built reports in May 2026, which may close part of that gap.
-   **Premium features despite all-inclusive marketing.** Some reviewers note capabilities reserved for the enterprise tier, which clashes with the "unlimited everything" positioning.
-   **Limited career-site customization.** The builder gets strong marks for ease of use, but reviewers say deeper customization runs out quickly.
-   **Scheduling and GDPR rough edges.** Reviewers report interview slots merging when several interviewers sync calendars, plus GDPR workflows that feel rigid. Neither is a dealbreaker, but both create manual cleanup.
-   **No AI-powered candidate sourcing.** Teamtailor is an ATS with employer branding tools. It doesn't source candidates from external databases. If finding candidates is your bottleneck (not just tracking applicants), you'll need a separate sourcing tool or a platform that combines both.

That last point matters. The platform helps you manage candidates who've already applied or been added to your pipeline. But it won't go find passive candidates the way dedicated sourcing tools do. For teams where top-of-funnel sourcing is the primary challenge, an ATS alone won't solve it.

## Who Is Teamtailor Best Suited For?

More than 13,000 companies in over 90 countries use Teamtailor, according to the company. Founded in Sweden, it has particular strength in Europe, and its US presence is growing but still trails European adoption.

Teamtailor fits best for small and midsize companies where employer branding is a genuine priority and hiring volume is steady. The career site builder is among the strongest in the mid-market ATS category, and teams not actively using it are paying for something they won't touch. Predictable hiring keeps you inside one tier; spiky or seasonal hiring gets expensive once the quote moves up. European teams also have an advantage: GDPR tools are built in, and Teamtailor's own security overview (September 2026) lists ISO 27001 and 27701 certification plus an annual SOC 2 Type 2 audit.

It's a weaker fit for fast-growing startups with unpredictable hiring surges. Large organizations that need deep workflow customization may run into limits, although Teamtailor now sells a dedicated enterprise offer for companies with 1,000+ employees. Teams where sourcing passive candidates is the primary bottleneck need a different tool. Buyers who want to compare costs before talking to sales will also find the lack of published pricing frustrating.

## When Should You Consider Moving Off Teamtailor?

Consider moving off Teamtailor when your bottleneck shifts from managing applicants to finding them, or when the renewal math stops working. Most teams that switch hit one of four triggers:

1.  **Sourcing becomes the constraint.** When inbound applications stop filling roles, no amount of career-site polish fixes the top of the funnel.
2.  **Hiring volume outgrows your tier.** Scaling from 100 to 1,000 employees usually means 20-30+ concurrent roles, which pushes buyer-reported pricing from Growth toward Enterprise.
3.  **Escalators compound.** After three or more renewals at 5-8%, you're paying noticeably more for the same product.
4.  **Reporting can't keep up.** Teams that need source-of-hire and cost-per-hire analysis often end up exporting data into separate BI tools.

### Is Teamtailor cost-effective for SMBs?

Usually yes, for a small business hiring a handful of roles a year with a strong employer-brand focus. Negotiated Starter pricing near $250-$400/mo buys unlimited users and a polished career site. Small businesses looking to scale quickly face less friendly math, since each step up in concurrent openings moves the quote up a tier.

### Teamtailor vs Workable: which wins for a branded careers site?

Teamtailor's career site builder is the stronger branding tool. By contrast, Workable publishes per-employee pricing from $299/mo and offers a self-serve 15-day trial. Brand-first teams usually prefer Teamtailor, while teams that want predictable, published pricing lean toward Workable.

### What if sourcing is the real bottleneck?

If the trigger is sourcing, you may not need to replace your ATS at all. Pin is the best fit for teams that want to keep their applicant tracking in place and add AI sourcing. It plugs into 120+ ATS integrations and saves recruiters 12 hours per week on sourcing and outreach.

## How to Negotiate a Better Teamtailor Contract

Most Teamtailor contracts have negotiation room. [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/teamtailor) (2026) notes that buyers often achieve below-list pricing, especially with competing quotes in hand.

Here's what to push on:

1.  **Cap the annual escalator.** Ask for a flat renewal rate or cap increases at 3%. The default 3-8% range is a starting position, not final.
2.  **Build in a job-slot buffer.** If you need 10 slots now, negotiate pricing for 15. It's cheaper than jumping a tier during a hiring spike.
3.  **Push for free onboarding.** Managed onboarding runs $1,000-$5,000, according to Vendr (2026). If you're signing a multi-year deal, ask for it to be waived or reduced.
4.  **Ask about multi-year terms.** Longer commitments are a common lever for a lower annual rate. Do the math against escalator costs to see if locking in is worth it.
5.  **Get competitor quotes first.** The sales team is more flexible when you have an active Workable or Greenhouse quote in hand, and Workable's published pricing makes a benchmark easy to get. The mid-market ATS space is competitive enough that switching costs work in the buyer's favor.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Teamtailor cost per month?

Teamtailor doesn't publish pricing, but [Vendr](https://www.vendr.com/buyer-guides/teamtailor) (2026) estimates list prices of $300-$400/month on Starter, $600-$1,200/month on Growth, and $1,500+/month on Enterprise. Negotiated deals typically land between about $250/month for small teams and $2,000+/month for large ones. Mid-market buyers usually spend $6,000-$12,000 per year in total.

### How much does the ATS system cost?

ATS costs vary widely by platform and pricing model. Workable publishes plans from $299/month, and Ashby's Foundations plan is $400/month for up to 100 employees. Teamtailor is quote-only, with mid-market contracts around $6,000-$12,000/yr according to Vendr (2026), while enterprise suites like Greenhouse and SmartRecruiters often exceed $12,000-$20,000/yr. Sourcing-first platforms like Pin start with a free plan and paid plans from $99/month.

### Is Teamtailor legit?

Yes. Teamtailor is an established Swedish ATS that says it serves more than 13,000 companies in over 90 countries. It reports ISO 27001 and 27701 certification and an annual SOC 2 Type 2 audit, and it holds a 4.6/5 rating across 113 Capterra reviews. The main buyer frustration is pricing opacity, not product legitimacy.

### Does Teamtailor offer a free trial?

Yes, but not a free plan. Teamtailor's trial typically runs 14 days and can be extended on request, and a sales rep sets it up rather than a self-serve sign-up. Once the trial ends, you'll need a paid, quote-based contract to keep using it.

### Who are the main Teamtailor competitors?

The closest Teamtailor alternatives in the mid-market ATS segment are Workable, Greenhouse, Ashby, and SmartRecruiters. Workable ($299/mo) is the most direct substitute, with a similar feature set and transparent per-employee pricing. Greenhouse and Ashby offer more advanced workflow customization, and Ashby starts at $400/mo. For teams that need candidate sourcing in addition to ATS features, Pin is worth evaluating: its 850M+ profile database, outreach sequences, and free plan offer a different cost structure than any of the above. Choosing depends on whether inbound applications or proactive sourcing is your primary hiring challenge.

### What's the biggest downside of Teamtailor pricing?

The lack of pricing transparency is the most-cited complaint. You can't see any pricing without contacting sales, making it impossible to compare costs before entering a sales process. Combined with 3-8% annual renewal escalators, an 8% clause lifts your price almost 17% above year one by year three.

### Does Teamtailor include AI candidate sourcing?

No. Teamtailor is an applicant tracking system with employer branding tools, and its AI Co-pilot works on candidates already in your pipeline. It doesn't source passive candidates from external databases. For AI-powered sourcing across 850M+ profiles combined with multi-channel outreach sequences, teams need a dedicated sourcing platform alongside or instead of an ATS.

-   Teamtailor is quote-only, with Vendr (2026) estimating $300-$1,500+/mo at list and $6,000-$12,000/yr for typical mid-market contracts

-   Hidden costs (onboarding, tier jumps, integration gaps, 3-8% escalators) push total spend above the first-year quote
-   Teamtailor's sweet spot is small and midsize companies with strong employer branding needs, especially in Europe
